# Agent docs — what a template ships for its next maintainer, and who writes each file

> **Phase 10 · Q1b packet.** Read at Q1b of `packaging-quickstart.md`, after the last content
> change and before the Akeeba capture. Pairs with `packaging-quickstart.md` §Q1b and
> `scripts/quickstart/gen-docs.sh`.

## Why a template carries its own documentation

A template that leaves this skill is handed to two readers who were not in the build: a human
maintainer, and the next agent — often in a Tracy Cowork session, with no access to the build
workspace, the spec-pack or this conversation. Everything they need to answer "what is this page /
block / position / token / command called here" has to travel **inside the template folder**, or
they will re-derive it from the DOM and get it wrong. The three ways that goes wrong while the
site still looks fine are the ones `tracy_business`'s `AGENTS.md` opens with: editing
`css/template.css` (compiled output — the next SCSS compile discards it), building a section as a
`mod_custom` (invisible to the ACM catalogue and to every recipe), and writing the DB directly
(no receipt, no undo, nested sets left broken). None of them raises an error.

## The tree

```
<webroot>/
  CLAUDE.md                       5-line pointer: "read templates/<tpl>/AGENTS.md first"
  AGENTS.md                       same text — two names because two kinds of agent look for two names
  templates/<tpl>/
    AGENTS.md                     the rules + "where things are" + layout of the template   AUTHORED
    README.md                     for people: where it runs, how to change things, status,
                                  hand-over checklist, licence                             AUTHORED
    docs/
      .htaccess                   Require all denied — nothing here is served
      index.html                  empty; stops directory listing where .htaccess is not read
      inventory.md                extensions, modules per position, plugins, custom fields,
                                  overrides — from #__extensions / #__modules            GENERATED
      site-map.md                 every published menu item per menu type with URL, view,
                                  style and association; categories, articles, tags,
                                  contacts — from #__menu / #__content / #__associations  GENERATED
      blocks.md                   the ACM catalogue: every block of this template with its
                                  admin form fields, and where it is used                 GENERATED
      positions.md                layouts row by row, page → style, every position with its
                                  purpose — from templateDetails.xml, etc/layout, #__menu  GENERATED
      positions.purposes.json     position → one-line purpose, merged into positions.md    AUTHORED
      design-system.md            tokens, type scale, spacing, bands, dark mode, don'ts     AUTHORED
      recipes.md                  how a change is made: add a page / block / article /
                                  menu entry / language string                           AUTHORED
      checks.md                   the commands that decide a change is done (compile, clear
                                  the T4 cache, render, audit)                            AUTHORED
      content-rules.md            what the source supplied, where it contradicts itself,
                                  what the owner still has to decide                      AUTHORED
      cowork-api.md               the com_claudecowork door: URL, where the token lives,
                                  actions, kinds, receipts and undo, a worked example      AUTHORED
      languages.md                what is installed, add/remove a site language           AUTHORED
      language-packs.json         data for tools/add-language.php / remove-language.php
    tools/
      add-language.php · remove-language.php
```

## Generated vs authored — and why the line is where it is

| | Generated (4) | Authored (6 + purposes) |
|---|---|---|
| Source of truth | the database and the template tree, **now** | the build's decisions and measurements |
| Written by | `scripts/quickstart/gen-docs.php`, at Q1b, last | the phases that made the decision (below) |
| Opens with | `<!-- GENERATED by scripts/quickstart/gen-docs.php … Do not edit; regenerate. -->` | nothing — an ordinary document |
| When stale | after **any** content or template change | when a decision changes — rare, and deliberate |
| If edited by hand | overwritten by the next run, silently | that is the intended way to change it |

The split follows one rule: **anything the DB or the tree can answer is generated; anything only the
build knew is authored.** A hand-written site map goes stale on the first new article and nobody
notices; a generated design-system doc cannot exist, because the reasons behind a token are not in
any table.

`positions.purposes.json` sits on the authored side on purpose: a position's *name* is in
`templateDetails.xml`, its *purpose* is a build decision ("`sidebar-r` — right column beside the
component: news and kit sidebars"). Without the file, `positions.md` still generates, with the
purpose column empty except for `*-page` positions, whose purpose the name gives away — and the
run says so on stdout.

## Who writes the authored files, and when

| File | Phase that produces it | Q1b does |
|---|---|---|
| `design-system.md` | Phase 2 (design contract) → Phase 6 (tokens compiled) | re-read against `design-contract.json`; every token named must exist in `css/styles/` |
| `content-rules.md` | Phase 2 (content contract) → Phase 7 (content compiled) | list what the owner still has to decide — this is the hand-over of open questions |
| `cowork-api.md`, `checks.md` | when the build environment is set up (Phase 0–1) | confirm the door URL and the token location are the **customer's**, not the build copy's |
| `recipes.md` | Phase 5 (ACM blocks exist) → Phase 7 (content patterns known) | one recipe per kind of change the site actually has; delete recipes for blocks that were pruned (Q1a) |
| `languages.md` | Phase 9 (system pages and language packs finalized) | match `inventory.md` — every `pkg_*-*` in the inventory is either "site language" or "installed, not enabled — languages.md" |
| `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` | Phase 8b sign-off | the rules must name only files that exist; the "Where things are" table must match the docs/ listing above |
| `positions.purposes.json` | Phase 4 (layouts) | one line per position in `templateDetails.xml`; unknown → leave out, never guess |

**Authored does not mean free-form.** Each file has one question it answers (the tree above); a
fact that belongs to another file is a pointer, not a copy — copies are what go stale.

## Running the generator

```bash
# docker (the fleet and the local build stands)
scripts/quickstart/gen-docs.sh --container <label>-web-1 --template <tpl> \
  --base http://127.0.0.1:<port> --block-prefix <p> --layout-prefix <p> --base-template "<base name>"

# DDEV
scripts/quickstart/gen-docs.sh --ddev --template <tpl> --block-prefix <p> --layout-prefix <p>
```

| Flag | Says | Leave it out and… |
|---|---|---|
| `--template` | the folder under `templates/` | the script refuses |
| `--base` | the build copy's URL, printed in `site-map.md` for orientation | `live_site` from configuration.php is used, or `http://127.0.0.1` |
| `--block-prefix` | which `acm/*` dirs are this template's (e.g. `tb-`); the rest are listed at the end of `blocks.md` as leftovers unless a module uses them | every dir is treated as the template's own — fine after Q1a pruned the base |
| `--layout-prefix` | same for `etc/layout/*.json` | same |
| `--base-template` | the name printed in the leftover notes ("Inherited from Tracy Base") | notes say "the base quickstart" |
| `--purposes` | path **inside the runtime** to the purposes JSON | `<tpl>/docs/positions.purposes.json` is used when it exists |

The script boots Joomla read-only (no identity, no session), reads, writes four files under
`templates/<tpl>/docs/`, and prints one line per file with the counts it found. It never touches an
authored file, and it refuses a template that has no default style — that is the sign it was
pointed at a template the site does not use.

**Order at Q1b, and the reason:** last content edit → `gen-docs.sh` → rotate the Cowork token and
the build admin (`packaging-quickstart.md` §Q1b) → Q2 capture. The backup takes the site as-is; a
generator run before the final edit ships an inventory that is one edit old, and `verify-parity.md`
will not catch it because both copies carry the same stale file.

## What the next agent is told

The root `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` pointer exists because an agent opening the webroot does not know
there is a template folder worth reading. `templates/<tpl>/AGENTS.md` then holds the rules — for
`tracy_business`, thirteen — and a "Where things are" table that maps every question to one file in
`docs/`. The rules that earn their place are the ones that name a way the site breaks **while
looking fine**: editing compiled CSS, building a section as `mod_custom`, writing the DB directly,
publishing one language of a pair. A rule that only says "be careful" is a sentence, not a rule.

## Checks before the capture

- `ls templates/<tpl>/docs/` matches the tree above; four banners present, six authored files present.
- `grep -l GENERATED templates/<tpl>/docs/*.md` lists **exactly** the four generated files.
- The generator's stdout counts (menu items, articles, modules, blocks, positions) match what Phase 8b
  signed off — a different number means content changed after review.
- `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' <base>/templates/<tpl>/docs/inventory.md` → **403**.
- `AGENTS.md` "Where things are" names no file that `ls docs/` does not show.
